note: Curated waypoint descriptions, keyed by the stable ids in data/waypoint-ids.json. Applied by scripts/build-trails.ts (overriding any description from the GPX source) and uploadable to the comments API with scripts/upload-descriptions.ts. Listed east to west, from Katoomba to Jenolan Caves, matching the km order of the generated trail data. Mount George has no entry: no source described it beyond a signpost. Descriptions give the permanent place; temporary closures are posted as server-side updates. Sources for each fact: plans/waypoint-description-sources.md.

descriptions.name: Pulpit Hill
descriptions.description: Hill at the Katoomba end of the track. On its side stood the Explorers Tree, a long-dead tree enclosed in 1884 to protect marks said to have been cut by Blaxland, Wentworth and Lawson on their 1813 crossing, a claim disputed for over a century. Transport for NSW removed what was left of it in February 2021, fearing it would fall.

descriptions.name: Katoomba (2 km east)
descriptions.description: The track starts by the Explorers Tree site on Pulpit Hill Road, about 2 km west of Katoomba, where there is parking. Katoomba has supermarkets, shops and the railway station. The route follows an 1884 horse track to Jenolan Caves, named for its width: six feet, enough for a horse-drawn vehicle.

descriptions.name: Six Foot Track Information Shelter
descriptions.description: Dirt car park off Nellies Glen Road with a shelter and a large Six Foot Track information sign, about 260 m along from the Explorers Tree site.

descriptions.name: Norths Lookout
descriptions.description: Fenced lookout a short detour from the track, looking over Nellies Glen into the Megalong Valley. Below it the track goes steeply down the Nellies Glen steps, beside high rock walls, crossing a small creek several times.

descriptions.name: Therabulat Lookout
descriptions.description: Clifftop lookout, also spelled Therabalut, with views over the Megalong Valley.

descriptions.name: Old Ford Reserve
descriptions.description: Campground just north of the Megalong Road bridge over Megalong Creek, about 500 m from where the track crosses the road. It has a wheelchair-accessible toilet, plenty of level ground for tents and access to the creek. Cars can drive in, and it sometimes has loud campers.

descriptions.name: Coxs River Camp Area
descriptions.description: Grassy campground on the west bank of the Coxs River, with a toilet, a sheltered picnic table and river access; fuel stoves only. Water is from a rainwater tank or the river, both untreated. Upstream, Bowtells Swing Bridge (built 1992, rebuilt 2024) carries walkers over the river; the ford below the camp crosses slippery rounded stones and is impassable in flood.

descriptions.name: Alum Creek Campground
descriptions.description: The least-used campground on the track, a flat grassy area in a sheltered gully beside the small Alum Creek; NSW National Parks lists no toilet. Water is normally in Alum Creek and in Little River, which the road fords about 750 m on, except in long dry spells. Past Little River the road climbs the Black Range with no water until the Black Range tank.

descriptions.name: Black Range Camp Ground
descriptions.description: Large fenced grassy campground on the Black Range, also reached by car, with toilets, sheltered picnic tables and an information board with a map; fuel stoves only. Its rainwater tank usually holds water, though long dry spells and vandalism have emptied it, and the water is untreated.

descriptions.name: Jenolan Caves
descriptions.description: The end of the track, reached down a steep, rocky ridge, narrow in places, overlooking the Blue Lake. The caves date back at least 340 million years, and the heritage-listed Caves House (1898) has restaurants, accommodation and a shop for essentials.
